The graph of a function $y=f(x)$ is shown above. It consists of two lines and the arc of a quarter-circle of radius $2.$ Given $g(t)={\int }_{-3}^{t}f(x)\,\text{d}x,$ determine the value of $g(0).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Evaluating $g(t)$ at $t=0,$ we get the following definite integral:

$$
g(0)={\int }_{-3}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x
$$

This integral gives the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis shown below.

 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14097009/assets/bc8905f82a9f7525d6c59df337138e9f3b0417a45bc40f4b76fee2ddedac2eab.png)

Note that the graph above consists of $2$ parts:

- $x\in [-3,-2],$ for which the region between the curve and the $x$-axis is a square. This corresponds to the area ${A}_{1}.$

- $x\in [-2,0],$ for which the region between the curve and the $x$-axis is a quarter-circle cut out of a rectangle. This corresponds to the area ${A}_{2}.$

Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
g(0)={\int }_{-3}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-3}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-2}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}
$$

Now, let's compute these integrals:

- To find the first integral where $x\in [-3,-2],$ we compute the area ${A}_{1}$ of the square as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & ={s}^{2} \\  & ={1}^{2} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

- To find the second integral where $x\in [-2,0],$ we compute the area ${A}_{2}$ of the quarter-circle cut out of the rectangle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =bh-\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =2\cdot 3-\frac{1}{4}\pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =6-\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}g(0)={\int }_{-3}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}=1+(6-\pi )=7-\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
